claim: Big Buddha Phuket reopened on 3 March 2026 for Makha Bucha Day after closing in August 2024; open 9am-6pm daily (last entry 5.30pm), entry free, dress code bans sleeveless tops and shorts above the knee; free sarongs available; best light is 4-5.30pm.
quote: Big Buddha Phuket reopened on 3 March 2026 for Makha Bucha Day after being closed since August 2024, and has stayed open since. 9 am – 6 pm daily (last entry 5.30 pm). No sleeveless tops or shorts above the knee.

claim: Wat Chalong's buildings are open 7am-5pm (grounds anytime); entry is free with donations welcome; shoulders and knees must be covered, shoes and hats off before entering buildings; early morning before 10am is coolest and quietest; allow ~1 hour; only 8 km from Big Buddha.
quote: The buildings are open from 7 am to 5 pm. The grounds outside can be walked at any time. Donations are welcome but not expected. Combine your visit with the nearby Big Buddha, just 8 km away.

claim: Wat Phra Thong in Thalang is famed for a half-buried gold Buddha that legend says cannot be fully excavated; open daily 8am-5.30pm, free entry, modest dress required.
quote: Wat Phra Thong is also known as Wat Phra Phud, meaning 'Temple of the Protruding Buddha'... it is believed that the Buddha was discovered by farmers who could only dig and uncover half of it.

claim: Wat Srisoonthorn (Wat Lipon) sits ~5km north of the Heroines Monument on Thepkasathri Road and is distinguished by a 29-metre gilded reclining Buddha on the upper floor; open 7am-5pm; early morning is least crowded; shoes off before entry.
quote: Wat Sri Sunthon (Wat Lipon) is a Buddhist temple in Thalang... the temple is distinguished by its massive reclining Buddha statue that stretches 29 meters long. The temple is open 7 am – 5 pm.

claim: The Heroines Monument at the Thalang roundabout honours sisters Chan and Mook who rallied Thalang's defenders against a Burmese siege in 1785; the bronze statue was cast by Bangkok's National Academy of Fine Arts and erected in 1966.
quote: Their bronze statue, cast by Bangkok's National Academy of Fine Arts and erected on the roundabout near Thalang in 1966, is perhaps the most photographed monument on the island.

claim: Chinpracha House is a 1903 Sino-Portuguese mansion in Phuket Old Town preserved as a private museum, open daily 8:00-16:00 with admission around 150 baht for foreign visitors.
quote: Chinpracha House Museum (Ban Chinpracha) - official Tourism Authority of Thailand listing.

claim: The Phuket Thaihua Museum, housed in a former Chinese school in Old Town, traces the Hokkien Chinese immigration and tin-mining era that shaped Phuket; entrance fee is 200 baht (50 baht for Thai nationals).
quote: the growth of Phuket's Chinese community and the tin mining industry they brought to the city... 200 Thai baht per person... 50 baht for Thai nationals.

claim: Operators routinely combine Karon Viewpoint, Big Buddha and Wat Chalong as an efficient half-day afternoon loop with ~1pm pickup and ~4:15pm return.
quote: Phuket City Tour with Big Buddha, Wat Chalong & Scenic Viewpoints - afternoon tours typically pickup around 1:00 PM and return around 4:15 PM.

claim: The official Phuket provincial site documents the Heroines Monument at the Thepkrasattri/Srisoonthorn road junction in Thalang as a tribute to Thao Thepkrasattri and Thao Srisoonthorn who repelled the 1785 Burmese invasion.
quote: Phuket Heroines Monument - official Phuket Province historical site listing for Thao Thepkrasattri and Thao Srisoonthorn.
